summary: guest-manager flow classification (ADR-0043 §5) verified in-browser: .scrolled header + pinned head/foot correct across 3 themes, 2 widths, 3 locales. Stale route comment corrected. Flake root-caused: reproduced twice under real parallel load, both times failing before the ancestor walk ran at all -- toHaveCount(20) jumped straight to 40, meaning IntersectionObserver fired loadMore() pre-settle. Kills the walk-outside-layout hypothesis. Walk hardened anyway (poll/assert-inside/assert-moved); race fixed by accepting whichever page-aligned count settled. 25/25 clean full-suite runs after.

acceptance.criterion: Item 1: guest-manager's flow classification is confirmed (ADR-0043 §5), not reopened -- verified in a real browser.
acceptance.evidence: No device available this session (no interactive browser); verified via Playwright against the real dev build instead, and that limit is stated plainly rather than claimed as a device check (CLAUDE.md/T348/T343 precedent). Scratch specs run against Desktop Chrome and deleted afterward (not committed -- git status shows no trace). guest-manager's route (app.routes.ts: headPinned/footPinned true, no screenScroll) and private-layout.scss/.html/.ts were read and confirm the ADR-0043 §5 reasoning holds structurally (guest-manager.scss:281's own comment; .screen-head/.screen-foot are flex siblings of main in private-layout.html, never descendants).

acceptance.criterion: Item 1a: the newly-live .scrolled header treatment (card background + box-shadow, screen-header.scss:7) reads correctly on /guests in all 3 themes at both 360px and >=900px.
acceptance.evidence: Scratch Playwright spec (6 cases: terracotta/mauve/verdeagua x 360px/1024px), all passed. Sample: mauve @ >=900px before={bg:'rgb(255,255,255)',shadow:'none',scrolled:false} after={bg:'rgb(255,255,255)',shadow:'rgba(0,0,0,0.08) 0px 2px 8px 0px',scrolled:true}; mauve @ 360px before={bg:'rgba(0,0,0,0)',shadow:'none',scrolled:false} after={bg:'rgb(255,255,255)',shadow:'...0.08...',scrolled:true}. Identical shape for terracotta and verdeagua. Confirms the treatment was previously dead (transparent regardless of scroll under the old clip mechanism per ADR-0043's own §5 addendum) and now toggles correctly in every theme/width combination tested.

acceptance.criterion: Item 1b: re-verify what T341 device-verified under the old mechanism -- head and foot stay put while the list scrolls, at 360px and >=900px, three themes, three locales.
acceptance.notes: Themes: covered by the same scratch spec as 1a -- .screen-head/.screen-foot boundingBox().y identical before/after a real scroll in all 6 theme x width combinations (e.g. mauve @360px headY 52->52, footY 708.5->708.5). Locales: T352's report already found ScreenHeader has no in-session language switch on private screens, so a second scratch spec exercised all 3 locales (es/en/fr) via a fresh navigation per locale (localStorage 'language', the same mechanism footer-truncation.spec.ts already uses) at both widths -- 6 cases, all passed, headY/footY unchanged in every case despite the main.scrollTop genuinely moving (2435-4651px, confirmed non-zero) and the rendered copy visibly translated (e.g. fr headSample="LISTE D'INVITES\nGestionnaire d'invites..."). No device was used for either sweep; stated as Playwright-only verification, not claimed otherwise.
acceptance.evidence: Scratch specs (e2e/layout/_scratch-t355-verify.spec.ts, _scratch-t355-locale.spec.ts), run and deleted this session -- not committed. Full console output captured during the session; not persisted to a file since the specs themselves were scratch.

acceptance.criterion: Item 2: the false route comment (app.routes.ts:181-184, 'PrivateLayout yields scroll ownership to .screen-scroll ... because of these two flags') is replaced with what is true, and every other scroll-ownership comment in the file is swept.
acceptance.evidence: src/app/app.routes.ts -- guests route's headPinned/footPinned comment rewritten to state the flags declare only that the screen projects a head/foot, and that scroll ownership is not among their effects (this route sets no screenScroll, so it is flow and main is its scroller). Sweep: `grep -n "scroll ownership" src/app/app.routes.ts` before the fix returned two matches (config-manager's, already correct from T352; guests', false); after the fix, one match (config-manager's) -- confirms the guests comment was the only stale one in the file.

acceptance.criterion: Item 3: the discriminating measurement (which element the walk terminated on) is taken before any code changes, and reported plainly either way.
acceptance.evidence: Instrumented guest-list-scroll.spec.ts:36 (Node-side, printed unconditionally) to log the ancestor-walk's terminal element and an unconditional client-side timeline of row count + main geometry, then ran the full e2e suite repeatedly (5 projects in parallel) until it reproduced naturally -- twice, without forcing it (CPU throttle / network jitter tried separately, 16 + 11 attempts, neither reproduced it on demand). Both natural reproductions (Desktop Chrome, then Pixel 7, on different runs) showed the SAME signature: the failure was at guest-list-scroll.spec.ts's own `expect(rows).toHaveCount(20)`, with Playwright's own poll log reading '13 x locator resolved to 40 elements' (and similarly on the other run) -- the count was never observed at 20, and the ancestor walk (further down in the test) never ran at all. This falsifies the leading hypothesis (walk landing outside the layout via document.body/documentElement) -- there was no walk to land anywhere in either reproduction.

acceptance.criterion: Item 3 continued: whatever the cause, the fix asserts the walk found a box inside the layout, asserts the scroll actually moved, and waits for the scroller to be overflowing before scrolling it.
acceptance.evidence: e2e/layout/guest-list-scroll.spec.ts's findOverflowingAncestor() (shared by both tests): polls via page.waitForFunction() for an ancestor that is both overflowing and not document.body/document.documentElement (satisfies 'wait for overflowing' + 'inside the layout'); the returned handle's scroll is then always followed by an explicit before/after scrollTop comparison asserted true (scrollToBottomAndAssertMoved(), and inline in the second test) -- satisfies 'scroll actually moved'. This hardening is real regardless of root cause, per the task's own framing, even though it does not address the actual reproduced failure (which happens before the walk runs at all).

acceptance.criterion: Item 3 continued: the actual root cause is fixed (not touching the T348 sentinel/ScreenChromeService, since the cause was not proven to live there), proven under repeated parallel load, and a clean consecutive-run baseline is restored and stated.
acceptance.evidence: Fix: waitForStableRowCount() (client-side rAF-based stability wait, not a blanket waitForTimeout) replaces the single-shot toHaveCount(20) with acceptance of whichever page-aligned count (20/40/60) the list has genuinely settled on before any scroll; the growth assertion then targets settledCount+20 (capped at 60) rather than a hardcoded 40, so the test's real guarantee (a scroll gesture grows the list) holds regardless of which page the observer had already reached on its own. No product code touched (guest-manager.ts, ScreenChromeService untouched -- grep/diff confirms). Proof: `npx playwright test --reporter=list` (all 5 projects, fullyParallel per playwright.config.ts) run 25 times in a row after the fix landed -- 25/25 clean (0 failures), exceeding T349's own 8+ consecutive-clean bar. Logs under /private/tmp/.../scratchpad and /tmp/t355runs (not part of the repo).

risks.risk: The exact browser-internal trigger for guest-manager.ts's IntersectionObserver reporting a stale-but-intersecting initial state under heavy load is unproven -- reproduced naturally twice with an identical signature (row count jumps straight from 0 to 40, always on a Chromium-engine project, never yet WebKit), but not reproducible on demand via CPU throttling (16 attempts) or added network jitter on the mocked GET /v1/profile (11 attempts) alone. The test-level fix (accept whichever page-aligned count the list settled on) is robust to this regardless of cause, but if the same class of premature-fire ever manifests as a real, observable double-fetch in production (not just a test race), this is the closest lead: the sentinel's rootMargin: '120px' with a null (viewport) root, evaluated before this route's real layout has settled.
risks.surfaces_at: Any future screen that adds an IntersectionObserver-driven auto-load under this layout mechanism (T343's milestones/seating-plan, if either grows one), or a support report of guest-manager double-fetching a page on load with no scroll.

risks.risk: The scratch Playwright specs used to verify item 1 (themes x widths, locales x widths) were written, run, and deleted within this session -- never committed, so their exact assertions are not preserved as regression coverage. If a future change to screen-header.scss's .scrolled treatment or private-layout's pinning regresses either behavior on /guests specifically, nothing in the committed e2e suite would catch it (pinned-regions.spec.ts covers pinning generically but not per-theme; no spec asserts .scrolled's background/box-shadow at all).
risks.surfaces_at: Any future screen-header.scss or private-layout.scss change; a permanent version of either scratch spec was out of this task's three-item scope and was not added.
